# togetherai_endpoint (Resource)

A dedicated inference endpoint: the stable name clients send requests to (`model = qualified_name`). Add `togetherai_deployment` resources to run a model on it, and a `togetherai_endpoint_traffic_split` to route requests to them. This resource does not manage the traffic split, so a split set by another resource, the CLI or the console is not drift here.

**Cost:** an endpoint on its own does not bill. Deployments bill per running replica.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "togetherai_endpoint" "chat" {
  name = "chat"
}

# Clients send requests with model = this value.
output "endpoint_name" {
  value = togetherai_endpoint.chat.qualified_name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Endpoint name, either bare (`chat`) or qualified with the project slug (`my-project/chat`). Updated in place; this changes the name clients use.

### Optional

- `project_id` (String) Project that owns the endpoint. Defaults to the provider's project. Changing it replaces the endpoint.
- `visibility` (String) `VISIBILITY_PRIVATE` (project only, the default) or `VISIBILITY_INTERNAL` (shared with the organization). Updated in place.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time.
- `endpoint_type` (String) Serving class, such as `ENDPOINT_TYPE_DEDICATED`.
- `id` (String) Endpoint ID.
- `qualified_name` (String) Project-qualified name `<project_slug>/<name>`. Pass it as `model` in inference requests to `https://api-inference.together.ai`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an endpoint in the provider's project by its ID...
terraform import togetherai_endpoint.chat <endpoint_id>

# ...or in another project.
terraform import togetherai_endpoint.chat <project_id>/<endpoint_id>
```
